'''Herschel Shmoikel Pinchas Yerucham Krustofsky''',<ref name="Tablet">{{cite magazine |last=Leibovitz |first=Liel |title=The Problem With 'The Problem With Apu' |url=https://www.tabletmag.com/sections/arts-letters/articles/the-problem-with-the-problem-with-apu |magazine=[[Tablet (magazine)|Tablet]] |date=December 15, 2017 |access-date=August 23, 2026 |quote=Born Herschel Shmoikel Pinchas Yerucham Krustofsky on the Lower East Side of Springfield, the show's celebrated clown is the son of a rabbi, Hyman.}}</ref> better known by his stage name '''Krusty the Clown''', is a recurring character in the animated television series ''[[The Simpsons]]''. Voiced by [[Dan Castellaneta]], he is the longtime [[clown]] host of [[Bart Simpson|Bart]] and [[Lisa Simpson|Lisa]]'s favorite [[variety show]] featuring child-friendly [[Sketch comedy|sketches]] and often highly violent cartoons, most notably ''[[The Itchy & Scratchy Show]]''. Despite his cheery onscreen persona, Krusty is a cynical, burned-out, addiction-riddled smoker. He has been the focus of many episodes, including some about his relationship with former co-star [[Sideshow Bob]], who later became a major antagonist.

Krusty was created by cartoonist [[Matt Groening]] and partially inspired by [[James H. Allen|Rusty Nails]], a television clown from Groening's [[Portland, Oregon|hometown]]. He was designed to resemble [[Homer Simpson]] in clown makeup because Groening originally planned to reveal Krusty as Homer’s secret identity. Krusty made his television debut in the ''[[The Tracey Ullman Show|Tracey Ullman Show]]'' [[The Simpsons shorts|short]] "The Krusty the Clown Show".

The character was the favorite of several writers. Castellaneta won a [[Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Voice-Over Performance|Primetime Emmy Award]] for voicing Krusty and several other characters, and critics have praised the character's [[pathos]] and Krusty-centered episodes for their [[satire]] of Hollywood.

==Role in ''The Simpsons''==
Krusty was raised on the [[Lower East Side]] of [[Springfield (The Simpsons)|Springfield]] as the son of [[Rabbi]] [[Hyman Krustofsky]].<ref name="TOI">{{cite news |last=Suskind |first=Alex |title='The Simpsons' Celebrates 30 Years of Cartoon Chutzpah |url=https://www.timesofisrael.com/the-simpsons-celebrates-30-years-of-cartoon-chutzpah/ |work=[[The Times of Israel]] |date=June 8, 2017 |access-date=August 23, 2026 |quote=His parents ... land Stateside ... in "The Lower East Side of Springfield" ... where they look to raise their son.}}</ref> Little is known about his mother, Rachel, who died before the series' events.<ref name="CID">{{cite episode |title=Clown in the Dumps |episode-link=Clown in the Dumps |series=The Simpsons |series-link=The Simpsons |credits=Written by Joel H. Cohen; directed by Steven Dean Moore |network=Fox |date=September 28, 2014 |season=26 |number=1 |at=Krusty's family-photo album and Rachel Krustofsky's gravestone}}</ref> Hyman wanted Krusty to attend ''[[yeshiva]]'' and opposed his ambition to become a [[clown]], believing that [[show business]] would distract him from his faith.<ref name="TOI" /> It is later revealed that Krusty never had a [[Bar and Bat Mitzvah|Bar Mitzvah]] because Hyman feared he would disrupt the ceremony by "acting up."<ref name="TIAC">{{cite episode |title=Today I Am a Clown |episode-link=Today I Am a Clown |series=The Simpsons |series-link=The Simpsons |credits=Written by Joel H. Cohen; directed by Nancy Kruse |network=Fox |date=December 7, 2003 |season=15 |number=6 |time=08:18 |quote=Hyman: "I was afraid you'd make a mockery out of the whole ceremony."}}</ref> Krusty first performed [[slapstick|slapstick comedy]] in secret. At a rabbis' convention, a rabbi jokingly squirted him with [[carbonated water|seltzer]], washing off his clown makeup and revealing his identity to Hyman. Hyman then disowned him, and they did not speak for 25 years.<ref name="LFLC">{{cite episode |title=Like Father, Like Clown |episode-link=Like Father, Like Clown |series=The Simpsons |series-link=The Simpsons |credits=Written by Jay Kogen and Wallace Wolodarsky; directed by Jeffrey Lynch and Brad Bird |network=Fox |date=October 24, 1991 |season=3 |number=6 |time=09:57 |quote=Hyman: "You have brought shame on our family. I never want to see you again."}}</ref><ref name="Diner">{{cite book |last=Diner |first=Hasia R. |author-link=Hasia Diner |chapter=The Texts of Memory: Representations of the Lower East Side |title=Lower East Side Memories: A Jewish Place in America |publisher=[[Princeton University Press]] |location=Princeton, New Jersey |year=2000 |pages=53–55 |isbn=978-0-691-00747-2 |doi=10.2307/j.ctv173f04c.6 |doi-access=free |jstor=j.ctv173f04c.6 |quote=This episode of The Simpsons, "Like Father, Like Clown," showed how the Lower East Side had come to be universally understood as the epicenter of the American Jewish experience.}}</ref> After leaving Springfield's Lower East Side, Krusty begins his show-business career as a [[mime artist|street mime]] in [[Tupelo, Mississippi]].<ref name="KGB">{{cite episode |title=Krusty Gets Busted |episode-link=Krusty Gets Busted |series=The Simpsons |series-link=The Simpsons |credits=Written by Jay Kogen and Wallace Wolodarsky; directed by Brad Bird |network=Fox |date=April 29, 1990 |season=1 |number=12 |time=07:20 |quote=Bart: "He's my idol. I've based my whole life on Krusty's teachings."}}</ref>

Krusty later reconciled with his father with help from [[Bart Simpson|Bart]] and [[Lisa Simpson|Lisa]].<ref name="LFLC" /> As an adult, Krusty holds two Bar Mitzvahs: first a televised spectacle at Springfield Stadium intended to revive his canceled show, and later a simple ceremony designed to reconnect him with his father.<ref name="TIAC" /> Krusty later discovers that he has a daughter, [[Sophie Krustofsky|Sophie]], from a brief relationship with a [[Gulf War]] soldier, and the two begin to bond.<ref name="ICP">{{cite episode |title=Insane Clown Poppy |episode-link=Insane Clown Poppy |series=The Simpsons |series-link=The Simpsons |credits=Written by John Frink and Don Payne; directed by Bob Anderson |network=Fox |date=November 12, 2000 |season=12 |number=3 |time=07:27 |quote=Sophie: "I'm your daughter." Later: "You met my mom during the Gulf War."}}</ref>

Krusty hosts ''The Krusty the Clown Show'' on Springfield's Channel 6. Aimed at children, it has many devoted viewers, including Bart and Lisa.<ref name="KGB" /> In one episode, the Springfield program is described as the least popular version in the world.<ref name="YS">{{cite episode |title=Yellow Subterfuge |episode-link=Yellow Subterfuge |series=The Simpsons |series-link=The Simpsons |credits=Written by Joel H. Cohen; directed by Bob Anderson |network=Fox |date=December 8, 2013 |season=25 |number=7 |time=16:59 |quote=Lisa: "You are now the least popular Krusty in the world."}}</ref> Clips from 1961 and 1963 show Krusty interviewing [[AFL–CIO]] president [[George Meany]] about [[collective bargaining]] agreements<ref name="BoD">{{cite episode |title=Bart of Darkness |episode-link=Bart of Darkness |series=The Simpsons |series-link=The Simpsons |credits=Written by Dan McGrath; directed by Jim Reardon |network=Fox |date=September 4, 1994 |season=6 |number=1 |time=10:12 |quote=Krusty: "Tonight my guest is AFL-CIO chairman George Meany, who will be discussing collective bargaining agreements."}}</ref> and dumping snow on [[Robert Frost]].<ref name="SC">{{cite episode |title=Selma's Choice |episode-link=Selma's Choice |series=The Simpsons |series-link=The Simpsons |credits=Written by Jon Vitti; directed by Carlos Baeza |network=Fox |date=January 21, 1993 |season=4 |number=13 |time=06:49 |quote=Krusty: "I would like to start by reading a passage from Robert Frost."}}</ref> In 1973, Krusty performed a drugged-out version of [[The Doors]]' ''[[Break On Through (To the Other Side)|Break on Through (To the Other Side)]]''.<ref name="ILL">{{cite episode |title=I Love Lisa |episode-link=I Love Lisa |series=The Simpsons |series-link=The Simpsons |credits=Written by Frank Mula; directed by Wes Archer |network=Fox |date=February 11, 1993 |season=4 |number=15 |time=14:26 |quote=Krusty: "Break on through to the other side."}}</ref> By the 1980s, the show had become a children's program, although Krusty also provided updates on the [[1982 invasion of the Falkland Islands|1982 Argentine invasion of the Falkland Islands]].<ref name="BH">{{cite episode |title=Burns' Heir |episode-link=Burns' Heir |series=The Simpsons |series-link=The Simpsons |credits=Written by Jace Richdale; directed by Mark Kirkland |network=Fox |date=April 14, 1994 |season=5 |number=18 |time=10:47 |quote=Krusty: "The Falkland Islands have just been invaded. I repeat, the Falklands have just been invaded!"}}</ref>

Its recurring cast includes [[Sideshow Mel]], Tina Ballerina, and Corporal Punishment,<ref name="ISM">{{cite episode |title=Itchy & Scratchy & Marge |episode-link=Itchy & Scratchy & Marge |series=The Simpsons |series-link=The Simpsons |credits=Written by John Swartzwelder; directed by Jim Reardon |network=Fox |date=December 20, 1990 |season=2 |number=9 |time=09:26 |quote=Krusty: "Krusty will have to bring out his old friend Corporal Punishment again."}}</ref> as well as [[List of recurring The Simpsons characters#Mr. Teeny|Mr. Teeny]].<ref name="DotJ">{{cite episode |title=Day of the Jackanapes |episode-link=Day of the Jackanapes |series=The Simpsons |series-link=The Simpsons |credits=Written by Al Jean; directed by Michael Marcantel |network=Fox |date=February 18, 2001 |season=12 |number=13 |time=21:17 |quote=Krusty: "Every time you try to kill me, my ratings go through the roof, you nut!"}}</ref> [[Sideshow Bob]] begins the series as Krusty's main [[sidekick]]. Years of abuse eventually lead Bob to frame Krusty for [[Armed robbery|armed robbery]], but Bart exposes the scheme.<ref name="KGB" /> Bob later attempts to kill Krusty during one of Krusty's retirements, but the two reconcile; Krusty remarks that Bob's attacks boost his ratings.<ref name="DotJ" /> Sideshow Mel succeeds Bob and remains loyal despite enduring similar abuse.<ref name="KGK">{{cite episode |title=Krusty Gets Kancelled |episode-link=Krusty Gets Kancelled |series=The Simpsons |series-link=The Simpsons |credits=Written by John Swartzwelder; directed by David Silverman |network=Fox |date=May 13, 1993 |season=4 |number=22 |quote=Krusty: "I don't know how to thank you kids."}}</ref>

Bart is one of Krusty's biggest fans. In the episode "[[Krusty Gets Busted]]", he declares, "I've based my whole life on Krusty's teachings,"<ref name="KGB" /> and sleeps in a room filled with Krusty merchandise. At [[Kamp Krusty]], Bart becomes disillusioned when he discovers that the poorly run camp has little connection to Krusty beyond licensing his image.<ref name="KK">{{cite episode |title=Kamp Krusty |episode-link=Kamp Krusty |series=The Simpsons |series-link=The Simpsons |credits=Written by David M. Stern; directed by Mark Kirkland |network=Fox |date=September 24, 1992 |season=4 |number=1 |time=20:38 |quote=Bart: "How could you, Krusty? I'd never lend my name to an inferior product."}}</ref>{{sfn|Turner|2004|pp=128–129}} He exposes Sideshow Bob's plot to frame Krusty,<ref name="KGB" /> [[Krusty Gets Kancelled|helps revive Krusty's career with a comeback special]],<ref name="KGK" /> and [[Like Father, Like Clown|reunites him with his estranged father]].<ref name="LFLC" />

Krusty licenses his name and image for a wide range of substandard products and services, from Krusty [[alarm clocks]] to Krusty [[crowd control barrier]]s,<ref name="HtC">{{cite episode |title=Homie the Clown |episode-link=Homie the Clown |series=The Simpsons |series-link=The Simpsons |credits=Written by John Swartzwelder; directed by David Silverman |network=Fox |date=February 12, 1995 |season=6 |number=15 |time=02:35 |quote=Krusty's accountant: "You've already merchandised everything: Krusty's Monopoly Game, the Krusty Krowd Kontrol Barrier..."}}</ref> many of which are dangerous.<ref name="KK" /><ref name="Booker">{{cite book |last=Booker |first=M. Keith |title=Drawn to Television: Prime-Time Animation from ''The Flintstones'' to ''Family Guy'' |publisher=[[Praeger Publishers|Praeger]] |location=Westport, Connecticut |year=2006 |pages=54–55 |isbn=978-0-275-99019-0 |doi=10.5040/9798400642425 |quote=Krusty the Clown is the kingpin of a vast merchandising empire that specializes in poor-quality merchandise, often dangerous to children.}}</ref> In [['Round Springfield|one episode]], every box of [[Krusty-O's]], a [[cereal]] sold under his name, contains a jagged metal Krusty-O. Bart accidentally eats one and requires surgery to remove his [[Vermiform appendix|appendix]].<ref name="RS">{{cite episode |title='Round Springfield |episode-link='Round Springfield |series=The Simpsons |series-link=The Simpsons |credits=Story by Al Jean and Mike Reiss; teleplay by Joshua Sternin and Jeffrey Ventimilia; directed by Steven Dean Moore |network=Fox |date=April 30, 1995 |season=6 |number=22 |quote=Krusty: "It wasn't my fault. It was the Percodan." Later, Dr. Hibbert: "Bart, I found the culprit: a jagged metal cereal O."}}</ref> Krusty's licensing company, the "Krusty Korporation", also runs disastrous promotions and business ventures. During the [[1984 Summer Olympics]], it [[Lisa's First Word|sponsors a rigged promotion]] that backfires when the [[Soviet Union]] [[1984 Summer Olympics boycott|boycotts]] the games, costing Krusty $44 million.<ref name="LFW">{{cite episode |title=Lisa's First Word |episode-link=Lisa's First Word |series=The Simpsons |series-link=The Simpsons |credits=Written by Jeff Martin; directed by Mark Kirkland |network=Fox |date=December 3, 1992 |season=4 |number=10 |time=13:32 |quote=Krusty's accountant: "You personally stand to lose $44 million."}}</ref> Krusty also owns and serves as the mascot of the fast-food chain [[Krusty Burger]], where abandoned, half-eaten burgers are stapled together for reuse.<ref name="SMWIMtS">{{cite episode |title='Scuse Me While I Miss the Sky |episode-link='Scuse Me While I Miss the Sky |series=The Simpsons |series-link=The Simpsons |credits=Written by Dan Greaney and Allen Glazier; directed by Steven Dean Moore |network=Fox |date=March 30, 2003 |season=14 |number=16 |time=01:44 |quote=Declan Desmond: "Your customers may be shocked by my footage of you stapling together abandoned, half-eaten burgers."}}</ref>

Krusty spends his money almost as quickly as he earns it. He lights his [[cigarette]]s with [[United States one hundred-dollar bill|hundred-dollar bills]],<ref name="HtC" /> spends lavishly on [[pornographic magazine]]s,<ref name="BtF">{{cite episode |title=Bart the Fink |episode-link=Bart the Fink |series=The Simpsons |series-link=The Simpsons |credits=Story by Bob Kushell; teleplay by John Swartzwelder; directed by Jim Reardon |network=Fox |date=February 11, 1996 |season=7 |number=15 |time=19:21 |quote=Krusty: "That's why I faked my death."}}</ref> and loses fortunes by [[gambling]] on [[Horse racing|horse races]].<ref name="HtC" />

Krusty is a jaded show-business veteran who frequently gambles, smokes, and drinks.<ref name="BozoLAT">{{cite news |last=Bravin |first=Jess |title=Sometimes It Pays to Be a Real Clown. Just Ask Bozo |url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1995-12-30-ca-19241-story.html |url-access=limited |work=[[Los Angeles Times]] |date=December 30, 1995 |access-date=August 23, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210824231403/https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1995-12-30-ca-19241-story.html |archive-date=August 24, 2021 |url-status=live |quote=a shameless, cynical huckster who drinks, smokes and gambles when he's off the air.}}</ref> He has also abused [[Oxycodone|Percodan]]<ref name="RS" /> and uses [[Pepto-Bismol]] and [[alprazolam|Xanax]].<ref name="MSGtW">{{cite episode |title=Mr. Spritz Goes to Washington |episode-link=Mr. Spritz Goes to Washington |series=The Simpsons |series-link=The Simpsons |credits=Written by John Swartzwelder; directed by Lance Kramer |network=Fox |date=March 9, 2003 |season=14 |number=14 |time=15:21 |quote=Krusty: "And I'm on Pepto and Xanax." Later: "I'd like to introduce a bill banning air travel over residential areas."}}</ref> He becomes [[depression (mood)|depressed]] as soon as the cameras stop rolling.<ref name="TSA">{{cite episode |title=The Sweetest Apu |episode-link=The Sweetest Apu |series=The Simpsons |series-link=The Simpsons |credits=Written by John Swartzwelder; directed by Matthew Nastuk |network=Fox |date=May 5, 2002 |season=13 |number=19 |time=13:55 |quote=Marge: "Off camera, he's a desperately unhappy man."}}</ref> In ''[[Planet Simpson]]'', [[Chris Turner (author)|Chris Turner]] describes Krusty as "the wizened veteran, the total pro" who depends on celebrity despite his misery.{{sfn|Turner|2004|pp=392–394}} In "[[Bart the Fink]]", Krusty fakes his death after losing most of his fortune<ref name="BtF" /> but returns when Bart points out that leaving show business would mean surrendering his celebrity status.<ref name="BtF" />{{sfn|Turner|2004|pp=392–394}}

In "[[Mr. Spritz Goes to Washington]]", Krusty runs for [[United States Congress|Congress]] as a [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] in a campaign that satirizes partisan news coverage.<ref>{{cite book |last=Henry |first=Matthew A. |chapter=“Entertain and Subvert”: Fox Television, Satirical Comedy, and ''The Simpsons'' |title=The Simpsons, Satire, and American Culture |publisher=[[Palgrave Macmillan]] |location=New York |year=2012 |pages=19–20 |isbn=978-1-137-02778-8 |doi=10.1057/9781137027795_2 |quote=This rather shocking announcement is then followed by a satirical attack on the bias in mainstream news media.}}</ref> After being elected, he passes a bill rerouting flights away from the Simpsons' house.<ref name="MSGtW"/>

==Characterization==
===Creation===
[[File:Krustys first appearance.png|right|200px|thumb|alt=Krusty with blue hair and a green shirt, holding a microphone beside Bart|Krusty in his first appearance in the ''Simpsons'' short "The Krusty the Clown Show"]]
Krusty first appeared in "The Krusty the Clown Show", one of the [[The Simpsons shorts|''Simpsons'' shorts]] from ''[[The Tracey Ullman Show]]''. The short first aired on January 15, 1989.{{sfn|Richmond & Coffman|1997|p=15}} The character was partially inspired by television clown [[James H. Allen|Rusty Nails]], whom ''[[The Simpsons]]'' creator [[Matt Groening]] watched while growing up in [[Portland, Oregon]].<ref name="NPR">{{cite interview |last=Groening |first=Matt |author-link=Matt Groening |interviewer=[[Terry Gross]] |title='Simpsons' Creator Matt Groening |url=https://freshairarchive.org/segments/simpsons-creator-matt-groening-0 |work=[[Fresh Air]] |publisher=[[WHYY-FM|WHYY]] |location=Philadelphia |date=October 23, 2003 |access-date=August 23, 2026 |quote=Krusty was based on a TV-show clown who I grew up with in Portland, Oregon ... named Rusty Nails.}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Barnes |first=Mike |title=James Allen, TV Personality Who Inspired Krusty the Clown on 'The Simpsons,' Dies at 87 |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/tv/tv-news/james-allen-dead-simpsons-krusty-811814/ |work=[[The Hollywood Reporter]] |date=July 29, 2015 |access-date=August 23, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150802024751/http://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/james-allen-dead-simpsons-krusty-811814 |archive-date=August 2, 2015 |url-status=live |quote=James Allen ... portrayed the clown character Rusty Nails ... and served as Matt Groening's inspiration for Krusty.}}</ref> Director [[Brad Bird]] watched the same performer while growing up elsewhere in Oregon.<ref name="King">{{cite news |last=King |first=Susan |title=Staring 'em Down |url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-2004-oct-31-ca-incredibles31-story.html |url-access=limited |work=[[Los Angeles Times]] |date=October 31, 2004 |access-date=August 23, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230524094933/https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-2004-oct-31-ca-incredibles31-story.html |archive-date=May 24, 2023 |url-status=live |quote=Brad and I both grew up in Oregon and we were mesmerized by a local TV clown named Rusty Nails.}}</ref> Groening described Rusty Nails as a gentle clown whose program sometimes carried a Christian message, although he found the name frightening.<ref name="KGBCom">{{cite AV media |people=Matt Groening; Brad Bird; Jay Kogen; Wallace Wolodarsky |date=2001 |title=The Simpsons: The Complete First Season |chapter=Audio commentary for "Krusty Gets Busted" |type=DVD commentary |publisher=20th Century Fox Home Entertainment}}</ref> [[Dan Castellaneta]] based Krusty's voice on [[Chicago]] television performer [[Bob Bell (actor)|Bob Bell]], who had a raspy voice and portrayed [[WGN-TV]]'s [[Bozo the Clown]] from 1960 to 1984.<ref name="tvguide">{{cite magazine |last=Rhodes |first=Joe |title=Flash! 24 Simpsons Stars Reveal Themselves |magazine=[[TV Guide]] |date=October 21, 2000 |volume=48 |issue=43 |pages=17–24, 26, 28, 30–33 |quote=Castellaneta modeled the voice after Bob Bell, Chicago's long-standing Bozo the Clown on WGN.}}</ref><ref name="Zimmerman">{{cite web |last=Zimmerman |first=Barak |title=Send In the Clowns |url=https://www.televisionacademy.com/sites/default/files/Downloads/clowns-infographic-2014.pdf |website=[[Television Academy]] |date=October 21, 2014 |access-date=August 23, 2026 |quote=Dan Castellaneta ... based the raspy voice on Bob Bell's version of Bozo.}}</ref> Groening praised Castellaneta's voice work, saying that he had to leave the room whenever Castellaneta recorded as Krusty to avoid ruining the take.<ref>{{cite AV media |people=Matt Groening |date=2003 |title=The Simpsons: The Complete Third Season |chapter=Audio commentary for "Treehouse of Horror II" |type=DVD commentary |publisher=20th Century Fox Home Entertainment}}</ref> Krusty has also been compared with "Flunky the Late Night Viewer Mail Clown".<ref>{{cite news |last=Zinoman |first=Jason |title=The Tears (and Fears) of a Clown |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2016/02/23/arts/the-tears-and-fears-of-a-clown.html |url-access=limited |work=[[The New York Times]] |date=February 22, 2016 |access-date=August 23, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160226161936/http://www.nytimes.com/2016/02/23/arts/the-tears-and-fears-of-a-clown.html |archive-date=February 26, 2016 |url-status=live |quote=The dissolute, depressive Krusty (Dan Castellaneta), a smoking clown like Flunky, was a breakout star on “The Tracey Ullman Show” and “The Simpsons.”}}</ref> The character was created and played by [[Jeff Martin (writer)|Jeff Martin]], who later joined the writing staff of ''The Simpsons''<ref>{{cite news |last=Hoffman |first=Ken |title=Houstonian Was the Man Behind Letterman's Flunky the Clown |url=https://www.houstonchronicle.com/life/columnists/hoffman/article/Houstonian-was-the-man-behind-Letterman-s-Flunky-6271565.php |url-access=limited |work=[[Houston Chronicle]] |date=May 18, 2015 |access-date=August 23, 2026 |quote=Jeff Martin, one of Letterman's comedy writers, created the character of Flunky.}}</ref> and wrote episodes featuring Krusty.<ref name="LFW" />

Film critic Eric Henderson described Krusty as the ''Simpsons'' character that "owes the biggest debt" to comedian [[Jerry Lewis]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Henderson |first=Eric |title=Jerry Lewis: The Clown Who Cried |url=https://www.slantmagazine.com/film/jerry-lewis-the-clown-who-cried/ |website=[[Slant Magazine]] |date=October 30, 2004 |access-date=August 23, 2026 |quote=The Simpsons character that owes the biggest debt to Lewis is Krusty the Clown.}}</ref> Asked about the resemblance, Groening said that "[''Simpsons''] characters are collaborations between the writers, animators, and actors".<ref>{{cite interview |last=Groening |first=Matt |author-link=Matt Groening |interviewer=[[Nathan Rabin]] |title=Matt Groening |url=https://www.avclub.com/matt-groening-1798209542 |work=[[The A.V. Club]] |date=April 26, 2006 |access-date=August 23, 2026 |quote=All of these characters are collaborations between the writers, animators, and actors.}}</ref>

Krusty's appearance is essentially [[Homer Simpson]]'s with clown makeup.<ref name="Booth">{{cite news |last=Booth |first=William |title=The Guys Who Go With the 'D'oh!' |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/archive/style/2007/07/25/the-guys-who-go-with-the-doh/d879002d-b276-47f5-b31a-fc3f1d04888f/ |newspaper=[[The Washington Post]] |date=July 25, 2007 |access-date=September 19, 2026 |quote="Krusty," Groening continues, "is just a clown version of Homer. ... The secret ... was that Homer was really Krusty in disguise."}}</ref> Groening said that "The satirical [[conceit]]<!--sic, please do not "correct" this without checking the source--> that I was going for at the time was that ''The Simpsons'' was about a kid who had no respect for his father, but worshipped a clown who looked exactly like his father", a theme that became less important as the show developed.<ref name="NPR" /> An early concept would have revealed Krusty as Homer's secret identity, but Groening abandoned the idea.<ref name="Booth" /> In the episode "[[Homie the Clown]]", Homer attends Clown College, dresses as Krusty, and is mistaken for him.<ref name="HtC" />
Krusty was originally conceived as an ordinary man wearing clown makeup, but [[David Silverman (animator)|David Silverman]] noted that "at some point, we decided he looked [like a clown] all the time".<ref name="tvguide" /> The producers debated whether Krusty should ever appear without his makeup but concluded that the distinction did not matter.<ref name="KGBCom" /> Although "[[Krusty Gets Busted]]" and "[[Like Father, Like Clown]]" showed what appeared to be his real face,<ref name="KGB" /><ref name="LFLC" /> the writers decided that he did not look right without his clown features. Later episodes turned the ambiguity into a joke. In "[[Homer's Triple Bypass]]", Krusty attributes his "grotesque appearance" to multiple heart attacks and insists, "This ain't makeup."<ref name="HTB">{{cite episode |title=Homer's Triple Bypass |episode-link=Homer's Triple Bypass |series=The Simpsons |series-link=The Simpsons |credits=Written by Gary Apple and Michael Carrington; directed by David Silverman |network=Fox |date=December 17, 1992 |season=4 |number=11 |time=16:09 |quote=Krusty: "Well, I got news for you. This ain't makeup."}}</ref><ref>{{cite AV media |people=Matt Groening; Al Jean; Mike Reiss; Michael Carrington; David Silverman |date=2004 |title=The Simpsons: The Complete Fourth Season |chapter=Audio commentary for "Homer's Triple Bypass" |type=DVD commentary |publisher=20th Century Fox Home Entertainment}}</ref> In "[[Bart the Fink]]", yellow makeup and black hair come off to reveal his natural white face and green hair, while removing his normal-looking fake nose exposes a naturally bulbous red one.<ref name="BtF" />

===Development===
[[File:Dan Castellaneta 2.jpg|right|200px|thumb|alt=Castellaneta wearing a cap and dark jacket, seated at a table|[[Dan Castellaneta]] (pictured) based Krusty's voice on Chicago television performer [[Bob Bell (actor)|Bob Bell]].]]
The [[The Simpsons season 3|season 3]] episode "[[Like Father, Like Clown]]" first establishes that Krusty is Jewish. His religion was not part of the original concept; writers [[Jay Kogen]] and Wallace Wolodarsky proposed the idea.<ref name="NPR" /> The episode parodies ''[[The Jazz Singer]]'', in which a son defies his father to become an entertainer despite his strict religious upbringing.<ref name="TOI" /><ref name="Diner" /> To complete the parody, the writers made Krusty Jewish and his father a rabbi. [[Al Jean]] proposed Krusty's surname, Krustofsky.<ref name="LFLCCom">{{cite AV media |people=Matt Groening; Brad Bird; Jay Kogen; Wallace Wolodarsky; Al Jean; Dan Castellaneta; Julie Kavner |date=2003 |title=The Simpsons: The Complete Third Season |chapter=Audio commentary for "Like Father, Like Clown" |type=DVD commentary |publisher=20th Century Fox Home Entertainment}}</ref> [[Jackie Mason]] played Krusty's father, Rabbi Hyman Krustofsky, and won a [[Primetime Emmy Award]] for [[Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Voice-Over Performance|Outstanding Voice-Over Performance]] for the episode.<ref>{{cite web |title=Outstanding Voice-Over Performance: 1992 |url=https://www.televisionacademy.com/awards/nominees-winners/1992/outstanding-voice-over-performance |website=[[Television Academy]] |access-date=August 23, 2026 |quote=Jackie Mason ... as Rabbi Krustofsky ... Winner.}}</ref>

"[[Krusty Gets Busted]]" establishes that Krusty is illiterate.<ref name="KGB" /> Subsequent episodes such as "[[Itchy & Scratchy & Marge]]" retained the trait, but the writers dropped it after the first few seasons because it limited the stories they could tell about him.<ref>{{cite AV media |people=Al Jean |date=2002 |title=The Simpsons: The Complete Second Season |chapter=Audio commentary for "Itchy & Scratchy & Marge" |type=DVD commentary |publisher=20th Century Fox Home Entertainment}}</ref>

For "[[Homie the Clown]]", the artists permanently revised Krusty's muzzle and added bags under his eyes to distinguish him from Homer.<ref>{{cite AV media |people=Matt Groening; David Mirkin; David Silverman; Mark Kirkland |date=2005 |title=The Simpsons: The Complete Sixth Season |chapter=Audio commentary for "Homie the Clown" |type=DVD commentary |publisher=20th Century Fox Home Entertainment}}</ref> In "[[Lisa's Wedding]]", set fifteen years in the future, the artists based an older version of Krusty on [[Groucho Marx]].<ref name="Daniels">{{cite AV media |people=Greg Daniels |date=2005 |title=The Simpsons: The Complete Sixth Season |chapter=Audio commentary for "Lisa's Wedding" |type=DVD commentary |publisher=20th Century Fox Home Entertainment}}</ref>

Several original writers identified with Krusty and considered him a favorite to write. His show-business role created opportunities for industry [[satire]], and many of his experiences and anecdotes draw on the writers' lives and stories they had heard.<ref>{{cite AV media |people=Matt Groening; Al Jean; Mike Reiss; David Silverman |date=2004 |title=The Simpsons: The Complete Fourth Season |chapter=Audio commentary for "Krusty Gets Kancelled" |type=DVD commentary |publisher=20th Century Fox Home Entertainment}}</ref> Krusty was a particular favorite of [[Brad Bird]], who directed the first two Krusty episodes and tried to animate at least one scene in every episode centered on the character.<ref name="LFLCCom" /><ref name="SalonBird">{{cite interview |last=Bird |first=Brad |author-link=Brad Bird |interviewer-last=Sragow |interviewer-first=Michael |title=Iron Without Irony |url=https://www.salon.com/1999/08/05/bird/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120615040525/http://www.salon.com/1999/08/05/bird/ |url-status=live |archive-date=June 15, 2012 |work=[[Salon.com|Salon]] |date=August 5, 1999 |access-date=August 23, 2026 |quote=He is my favorite Simpsons character ... For several seasons I'd animate at least one Krusty scene.}}</ref>

''Simpsons'' showrunners [[Al Jean]] and [[Mike Reiss]] planned an animated Krusty spin-off in which he would be a single father in New York City. The proposed supporting cast included a cantankerous makeup artist and a boss resembling [[Ted Turner]]. They later reworked the unsuccessful concept into the animated series ''[[The Critic (TV series)|The Critic]]''.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Reiss |first1=Mike |author-link1=Mike Reiss |last2=Klickstein |first2=Mathew |title=Springfield Confidential: Jokes, Secrets, and Outright Lies from a Lifetime Writing for ''The Simpsons'' |date=2018 |publisher=Dey Street Books |location=New York |isbn=978-0-06-274803-4 |page=209 |edition=1st}}</ref>

In 2015, ''[[The A.V. Club]]'' wrote that Krusty has "arguably the most [[pathos]] of any ''Simpsons'' character not named [[Moe Szyslak]]".<ref>{{cite web |last=McLevy |first=Alex |title=Krusty the Clown Tries and Fails to Stick It to the Man |url=https://www.avclub.com/krusty-the-clown-tries-and-fails-to-stick-it-to-the-man-1798185252 |website=[[The A.V. Club]] |date=October 11, 2015 |access-date=August 23, 2026 |quote=Krusty The Clown possesses arguably the most pathos of any Simpsons character not named Moe Szyslak.}}</ref>
''[[The Guardian]]'' called Krusty an "institution" and "icon", and described him as an important "narrative fulcrum" for [[Sideshow Bob]], the series' guests, and ''[[The Itchy & Scratchy Show|Itchy & Scratchy]]''. It also said that Krusty's many poorly made products amounted to "the most pointed satire" of ''The Simpsons''{{'}} own merchandising.<ref>{{cite news |last=Heritage |first=Stuart |title=Krusty the Clown: The Greatest ''Simpsons'' Character Ever? |url=https://www.theguardian.com/tv-and-radio/tvandradioblog/2014/jul/21/krusty-the-clown-greatest-simpsons-character |work=[[The Guardian]] |date=July 21, 2014 |access-date=August 25, 2026 |quote=Krusty the Clown ... is an institution. An icon. ... Krusty is an important narrative fulcrum, too.}}</ref><ref name="Booker" /> According to ''[[Time (magazine)|Time]]'', Krusty is a source of "showbiz jokes" as well as stories about "disappointment and living with one's limitations". It called his relationship with Hyman "something special" in a medium that "often ignores Jewish experience or writes it in as subtext".<ref>{{cite magazine |last=Poniewozik |first=James |author-link=James Poniewozik |title=The ''Simpsons'' Watch: Heaven, I'm in Jewish Heaven |url=https://time.com/3432718/review-the-simpsons-death/ |magazine=[[Time (magazine)|Time]] |date=September 29, 2014 |access-date=August 25, 2026}}</ref>
Philosopher Dieter Declercq argues that Krusty's merchandise embodies television's "phony commercial logic", which the series ridicules.<ref>{{cite journal |last=Declercq |first=Dieter |title=The Philosophical and Ethical Significance of Humour: ''The Simpsons'' as Humorous Ethical Truth-Telling |url=https://kar.kent.ac.uk/75355/1/04-Declercq.pdf |journal=Ethical Perspectives |volume=20 |issue=2 |year=2013 |page=292 |doi=10.2143/EP.20.2.2979754 |access-date=August 25, 2026 |quote=The personification of these commercial practices in Springfield is children's TV star Krusty the Clown and his plethora of merchandise.}}</ref> Sociologist David Feltmate calls Krusty "a stereotype that marks him as an ethnic, rather than a religious, Jew". He writes that "Jewish traditions mean little to Krusty except when he faces an identity crisis".<ref>{{cite book |last=Feltmate |first=David |chapter=The Difference Race Makes: Native American Religions, Hinduism, and Judaism |title=Drawn to the Gods: Religion and Humor in ''The Simpsons'', ''South Park'', and ''Family Guy'' |location=New York |publisher=[[New York University Press]] |year=2017 |page=88 |isbn=978-1-4798-9036-1 |doi=10.2307/j.ctt1ggjjmk.6 |doi-access=free |jstor=j.ctt1ggjjmk.6 }}</ref>
